subject: Criminal Law & Procedure

Question ID: 14697_manna_checkout
Transformed from: 14697

Peter went into Manna & Mustard Seed Bookshop, a privately owned Christian bookstore that also cashed small checks for customers. Peter tried to cash a $480 check that was payable to him. Mary, the clerk on duty, refused because Peter had only one form of identification, and the store’s policy required two.

Peter, who had no money except for the check and needed cash for food and a room for the night, became agitated. He put his hand into his jacket pocket and growled, “Give me the money or I’ll start shooting.” Mary recognized Peter as a harmless neighborhood regular. Feeling sorry for him, she counted out the cash. Peter left the check on the counter and walked out. Mary then noticed that Peter had not endorsed the check.

If Peter is guilty of any crime, he is most likely guilty of
call: If Peter is guilty of any crime, he is most likely guilty of
rightExplanation:
B is correct. Peter tried to obtain Mary’s cash by threatening immediate violence. That is the robbery frame. But Mary gave him the cash because she pitied him, not because the threat caused her to part with the money.

Gold Key: Completed robbery requires the taking to be accomplished by force or threat. If the defendant tries to rob, takes a substantial step, but the completed taking fails because the victim does not yield to the threat, factual impossibility does not defeat attempt liability.

Silver Key: When the array gives you robbery and attempted robbery, do not stop at the scary words. Ask why the property changed hands.

c3.text: Mary gave the money out of pity.
